public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 324

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/324](https://www.erdosproblems.com/324)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Polynomial

namespace Erdos324

/--
Does there exist a polynomial $f(x)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that all the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_324 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : ℤ[X], {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => f.eval (a : ℤ) + f.eval (b : ℤ) := by
  sorry

/--
Probably $f(x) = x^5$ has the property that the sums $f(a)+f(b)$ with
$a < b$ nonnegative integers are distinct.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_324.variants.quintic : {(a, b) : ℕ × ℕ | a < b}.InjOn fun (a, b) => a ^ 5 + b ^ 5 := by
  sorry

end Erdos324

sources_consulted: P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), §5, especially p. 53: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf
Ronald Graham publication index, 1980, entry 11: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/

review.notes: Checked both declarations; no mathematical mismatch found. Erdős–Graham, p. 53, asks for distinct sums f(a)+f(b) with a<b and explicitly proposes f(x)=x^5. The strict inequality and exponent were checked in the scanned original. Lean's injectivity condition expresses uniqueness of the increasing argument pair. Scratch proofs establish equivalence with the explicit four-variable condition, with nonnegative integer arguments, and between the quintic's natural-number arithmetic and evaluating X^5 over ℤ. Constant polynomials were proved not to satisfy the condition. Boundary tests include zero and exclude diagonal/reversed pairs; all 5,050 pairs with 0≤a<b≤100 produced distinct quintic sums. The scratch file compiles successfully without using the problem's sorry proofs. Source-access limitation: the cited erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare challenges despite descriptive User-Agent headers. The mathematical comparison therefore used the original book; the independent status database still lists problem 324 as open. The live site's latest remarks/status could not be directly checked.
